## About this exercise

You have a `references.bib` file in this project that already contains several entries. Together we will add two citations to the text below, render the document, and observe how the reference list is generated automatically at the end.

The two entries we will use are:

- `tilley2021my` (Tilley & Kalina 2021, "My flight arrives at 5 am, can you pick me up?")
- `kalina2023rich` (Kalina, Makwetu & Tilley 2023, "The rich will always be able to dispose of their waste")

## Our turn

We will work through Task 1 and Task 2 together as a live walkthrough. Follow along in your own copy of this file.

### Task 1: in-text citation

Edit the sentence below so that `@tilley2021my` appears as an in-text reference, replacing the underscore.

> In \_\_\_, the authors describe how visitors still expect a personal pick-up, despite the availability of taxi services.

Hint: the syntax is `@tilley2021my` (no brackets) when the author's name should appear as part of the sentence, like "as @tilley2021my describe...".

### Task 2: parenthetical citation

Add `[@kalina2023rich]` (with square brackets) at the end of the sentence below, before the period.

> Inequality underpins waste management systems, structuring who can or cannot access services \_\_\_.

Hint: with square brackets, both author and year appear in parentheses, like "...services [@kalina2023rich]."

### Render

Render the document. **Where did the reference list appear?**

## Your turn (stretch goals)

If you finish the walkthrough early, pick one of the two stretch goals below.

### Stretch goal 1: citation style

Add a `csl:` field to the YAML header to switch to APA formatting:

``` yaml
---
bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl
---
```

Re-render. Notice how the formatting of the references changes.

### Stretch goal 2: a richer scholarly YAML

For a real scholarly article, the YAML header carries much more metadata. Here is an example you can copy into a new document to see what is possible:

``` yaml
---
title: "An example scholarly article"
date: today
author:
  - name: First Last
    orcid: 0000-0003-2196-5015
    email: me@web.org
    affiliation:
      - name: ETH Zurich
        url: https://ethz.ch/de.html
abstract:
  The abstract will be placed here. Breaks can be added by hitting return on the keyboard.
license: "CC BY"
citation:
  container-title: My Blog
  url: https://www.example.com
bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl
editor: visual
---
```

Building a bibliography by hand is painful. Reference managers like [Zotero](https://www.zotero.org) (free, open-source) export `references.bib` for you.
